_readme: The writing systems as a tree over time (scripts/build-scripts.js, docs/writing-systems-plan.md). Each stage: its signs (strokes in a unit box, and an SVG path inked with its ductus), their values and what each came from; its changes, dated and named. The line and dates are placeholders for DJ to change.

painted.label: painted
painted.note: the first signs were pictures, drawn and painted before anyone cut them

incised.label: incised on bone
incised.note: a point on bone or wood cuts straight lines; curves become angles (Chinese oracle bone script, the runes)

chisel.label: cut in stone
chisel.note: a chisel likes straight cuts and leaves a small foot at each end (Roman capitals, early Greek)

stylus.label: pressed into clay
stylus.note: a reed stylus pressed into wet clay leaves a wedge at each push (cuneiform)

brush.label: brushed
brush.note: a brush thickens as it presses and thins as it lifts (Chinese regular script)

pen.label: reed pen
pen.note: a broad nib is thick across its edge and thin along it (Latin, Greek, Arabic hands)

cast.label: cast in bronze
cast.note: cut into a clay mould and cast: thick strokes, rounded ends (the Chinese bronze inscriptions)

relief.label: carved in relief
relief.note: cut in relief on stone, the picture whole, every curve kept (the Egyptian hieroglyphs on temple walls)

seal.label: seal script
seal.note: thin lines of one weight, curving, every sign in the same tall frame (the Qin small seal script of 221 BC)

song.label: printed, Song face
song.note: cut in wood for printing: thin across, thick down, a small foot at the turns (the Song typeface of the Chinese block printers)

leaf.label: on palm leaf
leaf.note: a point on a palm leaf must curve: a straight stroke splits the leaf (the round scripts of south India, Burma, Java)

roman.label: printed, with serifs
roman.note: the printed roman of the 1470s (Jenson): the pen's thick and thin made regular, with the chisel's feet

type.label: printed, sans-serif
type.note: the grotesque and geometric faces of the 1800s and 1900s: one even line, no feet
